Core exposure duration/intensity, stimulus timing and cortical acquisition/response settings remain a list to select later, without executable quantitative settings or a sufficiently specified calibration-to-setting procedure.

Animal/cluster replication and pilot variability are recognized, but no quantitative power or interval-width target is linked to the meaningful effect and independent-unit variance.
Contrasts and clustering are recognized, but the actual response/distribution model, assumption diagnostics and specified multiplicity policy remain incomplete.
Age, exposure dose and stimulus-parameter exploration has no bounded candidate grid or objective range-selection/search-stop rule before locking.
Troubleshooting does not explicitly connect technical changes to a revised frozen procedure and fresh independent confirmation; ordinary initial pilot separation is insufficient.

checks.quote: Minimum effect size or signal-to-noise threshold
checks.reason: An ODI formula is present, but the noise-derived denominator and weak/unresponsive-unit treatment remain generic thresholds to define; the main binocular fraction is conditional on responsiveness and can conceal group-dependent loss.

checks.quote: Imaging may be used as a secondary or alternative modality
checks.reason: Alternative imaging is listed without a defined independent/orthogonal confirmation comparison for the causal result.

Failure of diffuse light to rescue does not uniquely establish spatial instruction: retinal/cortical activity statistics and permissive requirements are not held equivalent by matching transmitted light alone.
